answer: Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the tide of payment, so volume alone buys nothing. The hollow holds work receipts rather than names, so the ripple of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. Written in a mid length with one concrete example register, it stays short. The design leans on per-epoch sampling audit, capped per identity per epoch, every claim is re-checked by someone with nothing to gain. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work.
